subject: GreenWave Renewal: Stability package & phased commit proposal
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Emily Torres <emily@greenwave.com>
Cc: procurement@greenwave.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning: options to preserve rate stability and enable growth

Emily —

Hope all is well. GreenWave’s current term heads into renewal in June, and given the strong usage patterns you shared last quarter I wanted to surface two pragmatic paths we’ve used with similar logistics customers to balance spend predictability with the need for capacity headroom: 

1) 12-month price hold + scaled commit (recommended)
   - Baseline commit = 1.2x current annualized usage
   - We hold current effective rate for 12 months against that baseline
   - One-time onboarding credit applied to offset migration/optimizations (suggested 6–10%)

2) Phased commit + shorter immediate hold
   - Start at 1.1x commit for first 6 months, move to 1.2x thereafter
   - 45-day true-up to smooth seasonal spikes

Both approaches include burst-capacity options, and we can layer a temporary overage discount for the first quarter if you want faster cost protection while you migrate traffic patterns.

If procurement wants a hard price-hold window and evidence of capacity, we can produce a term sheet and the usage export for Q1 (I can attach both). Can you confirm which path procurement prefers so I can pull the exact numbers?

Propose a 30-minute call next week to walk the term sheet and timing — I’m free Tue/Wed afternoons.

Thanks,
David
David Kim | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

Subject: Re: Renewal planning: options to preserve rate stability and enable growth

Thanks, David.

Quick context from my side: procurement is primarily focused on two things — a guaranteed price band for the next 12 months (we support longer commitments where the unit economics are stable) and a mechanism to avoid surprise overage fees during our Q4 peak. We also need a small credit to offset a tooling migration cost.

Can you produce: 
- A clean term sheet with the exact price per thousand tokens at the proposed baseline
- Q1 usage export (detailed by month and peak-hour percentiles)
- Confirmation of availability for burst capacity during a 48–72 hour window (we have a seasonal event in November)

If you can email the term sheet and usage export, I’ll loop procurement and get back with whether they prefer a single 12-month hold or a phased approach.

Emily Torres
Head of Data Platforms, GreenWave Logistics
emily@greenwave.com | +1 212-555-0198

Subject: GreenWave term sheet + usage export (draft)

Emily / Procurement —

Attached is a draft term sheet and the Q1 export you requested. High-level summary below so procurement can scan quickly:

- Baseline commit: 1.2x reported trailing-12 usage (annualized)
- Price hold: current effective blended unit price held for 12 months on baseline
- Onboarding credit: one-time 8% credit applied to first invoice after renewal
- Overage protection: 30% discount on any usage above baseline for first 90 days
- Burst pool: guaranteed access to extra capacity up to 150% of baseline in 48–72 hour windows (subject to 24-hour notice)
- True-up: standard 60-day true-up at quarter end (we can shorten to 45 days if needed)

Attachments (stubs):
- GreenWave_Renewal_TermSheet_20270419.pdf 
- GW_usage_q1_2027.csv

Next steps: 
1) Procurement reviews the term sheet and confirms preference for immediate 1.2x baseline vs phased 1.1x->1.2x.
2) If phased is preferred, we’ll substitute the onboarding credit for a staggered commit schedule and shorten the true-up to 45 days.
3) Once terms are agreed, I’ll circulate a DocuSign for countersignature (link included in HubSpot).

Happy to run a 20-minute review with procurement this week.

Best,
David

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: GreenWave term sheet + usage export (capacity/ops note)

David —

Quick operational read from the usage export and capacity planning: 

- Q1 peak-hour percentiles show sustained bursts during weekday mornings; migrating more traffic to streaming endpoints will increase KV-cache pressure by ~12%.
- Burst pool availability: we can commit the 150% burst for two separate 72-hour windows in the contract year without additional infra guarantees; anything beyond that will be best-effort and priced.
- Cost impact: a single immediate move to 1.2x baseline increases reserved spend ~18% OPEX vs current. Phased approach (1.1x → 1.2x) reduces immediate headroom to ~9% and is easier to operationalize.

Suggested changes to term sheet before sending to procurement: 
- Replace one-time 8% onboarding credit with a smaller 6% credit + a 45-day true-up (reduces credit exposure while giving short reconciliation window).
- Add explicit SLA fallback: if burst pool unavailable for a scheduled window, Redwood offers a 5% credit on that month’s invoice (subject to documented request 24 hours ahead).

I’ll model cost delta for both options and attach a quick spreadsheet if useful. Ben — can you confirm that engineering is comfortable with the outlined burst guarantees?

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Subject: Finalized proposal: phased commit + stability guarantees (adjusted per ops)

Emily / Procurement —

Following Monica’s ops notes, we revised the draft. Key changes and final proposal below: 

- Phased commit: 1.1x baseline for first 6 months, then 1.2x thereafter (reduces immediate reserved spend)
- Price hold: current effective blended unit price held for 12 months on the phased baseline schedule
- Credit & reconciliation: 6% onboarding credit applied to first invoice + 45-day true-up window
- Overage protection: 30% discount on overage for the first 90 days post-renewal
- Burst pool: two guaranteed 72-hour windows per contract year with 24-hour advance notice; SLA credit = 5% of affected month if we cannot meet the confirmed window

We’ve attached the updated term sheet and included a DocuSign link to accelerate execution: https://app.docusign.com/RENEWAL-GW-2027

If procurement approves, next steps are: 
1) Procurement confirms and signs via DocuSign.
2) Post-signature: Redwood will schedule a kickoff with Monica’s team to onboard and pre-warm the KV-caches (typically a 7–10 day ops window).

CC’ing Marissa for final approval on the credit/true-up tradeoff.

Thanks,
David
